checks.statement: The navigation rail should be placed vertically along the leading edge of the window.
checks.condition: When integrating a navigation rail: left for LTR content, right for RTL content.

sourceHistory.summary: Record the captured Container instruction without importing the exploratory audit assessments.
Preserve the source’s should recommendation rather than an unconditional imperative; confirm provenance against extractor version 2.

checks.statement: Always put the rail in the same place across screens of an app.
checks.condition: When the app uses a navigation rail.

checks.statement: The rail should contain 3–7 destinations, with an optional FAB.
checks.condition: When configuring primary rail destinations.
checks.notes: The guidelines apply the count specifically to the collapsed rail; expanded rails may reveal secondary destinations.

checks.statement: M3 Expressive introduces collapsed and expanded navigation rails.
checks.condition: When exposing design-generation availability for navigation rail variants.

checks.statement: The baseline navigation rail is no longer recommended; use the collapsed rail instead.
checks.condition: When choosing a rail configuration under M3 Expressive.

checks.statement: The expanded navigation rail replaces the navigation drawer.
checks.condition: When choosing the corresponding M3 Expressive navigation component.

checks.statement: Collapsed and expanded rails are available in M3 Expressive; the baseline rail is available in M3 and not recommended in M3 Expressive.
checks.condition: When presenting variant availability and recommendation metadata.
checks.notes: Read the complete variant table with the M3 and M3 Expressive column headers; -- denotes no listed availability.

checks.statement: The expanded rail supports standard (default) and modal layouts; M3 provides their predecessors as navigation drawers.
checks.condition: When exposing expanded layout configurations and generation availability.

checks.statement: Hide when collapsed is an M3 Expressive expanded-rail behavior.
checks.condition: When exposing expanded behavior configurations.

checks.statement: A collapsed or expanded rail destination contains an icon, active indicator and label; menu, FAB or extended FAB and badges are optional.
checks.condition: When composing an M3 Expressive rail.
checks.notes: Element list and diagram identify anatomy; detailed indicator and badge behavior is captured separately.

checks.statement: Use surface-container for the optional container, on-secondary-container for the active icon, secondary-container for the active indicator, secondary for the vertical active label, on-secondary-container for the horizontal active label, on-surface-variant for inactive icons and labels, error for badges and on-error for badge text.
checks.condition: When mapping collapsed and expanded rail colors in light and dark schemes.
checks.notes: Read the numbered diagram together with its nine color-role entries. FAB colors belong to the FAB component.

checks.condition: For collapsed and expanded rail destinations.

checks.statement: Represent enabled, hovered, focused and pressed states for navigation destinations.
checks.condition: When rendering collapsed and expanded rail items.
checks.notes: State diagrams show overlays for hovered, focused and pressed items; selection remains visible independently.

checks.statement: The menu button transitions between collapsed and expanded rails.
checks.condition: When a menu button is included.

checks.statement: The collapsed navigation rail should not be hidden.
checks.condition: When the collapsed rail is the selected navigation pattern.

checks.statement: Compact windows should use a navigation bar instead of a standard rail.
checks.condition: When choosing persistent navigation for compact windows.
checks.notes: Expanded modal rails can still open from menu buttons on mobile; do not treat this as a ban on modal expansion.

checks.statement: A navigation rail should be the only visible primary navigation element.
checks.condition: When using a rail; tabs may provide a separate navigation level.

checks.statement: Consider a navigation bar in medium windows with few destinations.
checks.condition: When choosing navigation for a medium window.
checks.notes: This conflicts with Resizing’s “Only use navigation rails for medium breakpoints and larger. Don’t use a navigation bar.” Preserve both instructions until resolved.

checks.statement: An expanded navigation rail should open from a menu icon.
checks.condition: When opening standard or modal expanded navigation.

checks.statement: An expanded rail may reveal secondary destinations that are not visible when collapsed.
checks.condition: When additional destinations are needed.

checks.statement: Place the standard expanded rail beside body content and the modal expanded rail over body content.
checks.condition: When choosing expanded rail modality.

checks.statement: Use a modal expanded rail for information-dense layouts with limited space or products with many navigation items.
checks.condition: When choosing standard versus modal expanded navigation.

checks.statement: The expanded rail may be hidden in immersive experiences and appear when the menu icon is selected.
checks.condition: When using hide-when-collapsed expanded behavior; the menu icon must remain accessible.

checks.statement: When the container fill is turned off, all rail items must retain at least 3:1 color contrast.
checks.condition: When rendering the rail directly on the surrounding surface.

checks.statement: The navigation rail should run vertically along the side of a layout; use a navigation bar for horizontal navigation.
checks.condition: When placing a rail in a page layout.

checks.statement: Rail destinations may be top- or center-aligned as a group; use center alignment on tablets.
checks.condition: When positioning the destination group for reachability.

checks.statement: The menu icon and FAB should always be top-aligned.
checks.condition: When either optional control is present.

checks.statement: The menu icon should change to indicate that the expanded rail can be collapsed.
checks.condition: When the rail is expanded.

checks.statement: A FAB nested in the navigation rail should have resting elevation level 0.
checks.condition: When an optional FAB is present.

checks.statement: Avoid placing the FAB below navigation destinations.
checks.condition: When an optional FAB is present.

checks.statement: Do not use a logo as the menu button for expanding the rail, and avoid logos that resemble actions or destinations.
checks.condition: When displaying branding at the top of the rail.

checks.statement: Use an active indicator only for the current open page, on no more than one destination at a time.
checks.condition: When displaying navigation selection.

checks.statement: The expanded active indicator hugs the label and icon; it may be overridden to fill the container to resemble the baseline navigation drawer.
checks.condition: When sizing the visible expanded active indicator; the target remains full width.

checks.statement: Navigation items must use icons that symbolize their destination’s content.
checks.condition: When choosing destination icons.

checks.statement: A selected icon becomes filled and changes color, with an active indicator behind it.
checks.condition: When selecting a navigation destination.

checks.statement: All navigation items require a short, meaningful one-word label describing the destination.
checks.condition: When authoring destination labels.
checks.notes: The same section permits line breaks or hyphenation when longer labels are unavoidable; retain that exception.

checks.statement: Avoid wrapping long labels where possible; if necessary, break between words or hyphenate longer words.
checks.condition: When a destination label cannot fit on one line.

checks.statement: Do not shrink label text or replace it with an ellipsis to fit more characters.
checks.condition: At default text size; accessibility guidance separately allows truncation beyond 2× scaling.

checks.statement: Place a collapsed rail’s badge at the icon’s upper right; an expanded rail’s badge should sit next to the label.
checks.condition: When showing count or status badges.
checks.notes: The prose says compact nav rails; interpret this as collapsed rail layout, not the compact window class.

checks.statement: An optional divider should be vertical and sit on the rail edge adjacent to app content.
checks.condition: When separating rail and body content with a divider.

checks.statement: The rail should sit outside body-content panes along the leading edge of the window.
checks.condition: When integrating navigation into an adaptive layout.

checks.statement: Body content may fill space vacated by a hidden rail as long as the menu icon remains accessible.
checks.condition: When hiding an expanded rail.

checks.statement: Use a navigation bar for compact layouts and a navigation rail for expanded to extra-large layouts; never show the bar and rail simultaneously.
checks.condition: When adapting navigation across window sizes.

checks.statement: Use a navigation rail at medium breakpoints and larger rather than a navigation bar.
checks.condition: When following the Resizing section’s medium-window recommendation.
checks.notes: Conflicts with Collapsed’s suggestion to consider a navigation bar for medium windows with few destinations; not resolved by this curation.

checks.statement: Consider a modal expanded rail when there are more than five destinations.
checks.condition: When choosing adaptive navigation for many destinations.

checks.statement: Page contents should adjust to fit when a standard rail expands.
checks.condition: When the rail expands beside content.
checks.notes: The prose says page contents should adjust on expansion; scope is interpreted as standard because the Expanded section defines modal as overlapping content.

checks.statement: The FAB should transition into an extended FAB as the rail expands.
checks.condition: When an optional FAB is present during expansion.

checks.statement: Use a standard expanded rail for secondary destinations or actions with lower priority than primary navigation.
checks.condition: When space permits an expanded rail beside content.

checks.statement: Rail destinations should remain fixed and visible while page content scrolls vertically.
checks.condition: When the body scrolls vertically.

checks.statement: A rail may stay fixed or scroll off-screen during horizontal scrolling; use a divider or rail elevation to distinguish content scrolling underneath.
checks.condition: When the layout scrolls horizontally beneath a visible rail.
checks.notes: The section describes level 1 as an elevation option; it does not require both divider and elevation.

checks.statement: Selecting a destination uses a top-level page transition and expands the active indicator from the icon’s center.
checks.condition: When a navigation destination is activated.
checks.notes: The linked transition-pattern page has not been captured in this run; detailed page-transition timing remains outside this check.

checks.statement: Predictive back applies only to the modal expanded rail and reveals the previous screen in a preview.
checks.condition: On Android with predictive back.
checks.notes: This platform-specific rule is not automatically a web requirement; applicability must be assessed separately.

checks.statement: People using assistive technology should be able to navigate destinations, select a destination and receive feedback appropriate to their input.
checks.condition: When interacting with the rail through assistive technology.

checks.statement: On selection, show the active indicator with a ripple, switch the icon from outlined to filled, and change icon and text color.
checks.condition: When tapping a navigation item.

checks.statement: Show a hover state to signal that a destination is interactive.
checks.condition: When hovering a destination with a cursor.

checks.statement: Active and inactive icon colors need sufficient contrast against the container; do not use low-contrast colors or more than two destination colors.
checks.condition: When choosing rail destination colors.
checks.notes: The section recommends the default scheme. The explicit 3:1 threshold for transparent containers is recorded separately; do not invent a new numeric threshold here.

checks.statement: Use semibold icon weight for an active destination when its icon has no filled style.
checks.condition: When the icon family lacks a filled variant.

checks.statement: Navigation items should grow vertically for larger text while retaining default padding; scaled labels may wrap.
checks.condition: When a device increases text size.

checks.statement: Keep the full destination label visible up to 2× text size; beyond that size it may truncate.
checks.condition: When testing device text scaling.

checks.statement: Initial focus lands on the first interactive item: the menu, FAB or first destination.
checks.condition: When keyboard focus enters the rail; this does not require stealing focus on page load.

checks.statement: Tab moves from the FAB or menu into the navigation items.
checks.condition: When keyboard focus is on a leading rail control.

checks.statement: Use a filled selected icon and outlined inactive icons rather than the same unfilled style for both.
checks.condition: When the icon family has filled and outlined styles.

checks.statement: Tab and arrow keys navigate interactive elements.
checks.condition: When using keyboard navigation within the rail.

checks.statement: Space and Enter select the focused interactive element.
checks.condition: When activating a rail destination with the keyboard.

checks.statement: The accessible name typically matches the visible label; use a more descriptive accessible name when the visible label is ambiguous.
checks.condition: When naming navigation destinations for assistive technology.
checks.notes: For example, Recent can be named Recent images. The section notes that Android Views lacks this customization and does not announce the role; do not apply that platform limitation to web.
